summary:
Interim report (audit continuing). No sign so far that anyone got in without authorization. All successful SSH logins on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 match staff accounts from their usual addresses, CI (10.20.0.30) or db-01's backup key. The deploy password logins from 35.196.129.99 are the old monitoring box: steady every few hours for 14 days, and they only run sudo larkspur-restart. Internet noise: password brute force against deploy, jpark, root and others from many IPs, none successful. Grafana file-read probes from 159.89.112.12 got 404s (8.3.1 is patched). mfischer logged in from a new mobile address (107.77.170.208) and did her usual newsletter export; it looks like her phone, and I'm still watching it.
Fixes so far: web-01: locked the former contractor jpark (in the sudo group with a password, not in the staff list, being brute-forced) and removed his WordPress administrator role. Removed deploy's sudo rsync (a root shell through rsync -e). larkspur-orders no longer runs the deploy-writable wp-config.php as root or evals its output. larkspur-mailing-export no longer writes/chowns as root in the user's home (a symlink there allowed overwriting any file as root). Removed the old agency's must-use plugin agency-support.php, whose ?asup=env needed no login and showed the database settings (kept in /root/disabled). ci-01: the repo config holding the GitHub token was world-readable, and config/hooks were developer-writable while root ran git gc on the repo (developer→root). Config is now root:developers 640 and hooks are root-owned; gc runs as deploy with hooks off. Release, dumps, payouts and settle all checked working.

Assessment changed: I believe Mia Fischer's (mfischer) web-01 password is being used by someone else. Evidence: password logins from 107.77.170.208 at 14:05, 14:09 and 14:13. In 14 days of logs she never used that address; she always logs in from 67.180.67.206, and she did so at 14:07, between the mobile sessions. The mobile sessions read the access log, exported the newsletter list (41 customers, names and emails) and printed the whole file (she normally looks at 5 lines), then ran `sudo -n -l` and `ls -la ~`, which looks like checking what the account can do. What I did: killed the sessions, rotated mfischer's password (rotate-secret staff-password; the help desk gives her the new one in about 8 minutes) and dropped 107.77.170.208 in web-01's firewall. Her keys and crontab are unchanged, and she has no files elsewhere. mfischer has no account on db-01 or ci-01, and the address never appears there. Her sudo is only the export tool; its symlink root hole (see below) was closed at ~14:09:40 and the export log shows it was not abused. She can read no secrets (payments.ini, backup and Grafana configs are root/grafana only), so no shop secret needed rotating because of this. Exposed: the newsletter customer list. Please confirm with Mia that it wasn't her, and consider telling those customers.
Not intrusions: deploy password logins from 35.196.129.99 (the old monitoring box; only sudo larkspur-restart), and internet brute force, Grafana probes and Tor traffic (all failed).
Weaknesses fixed: web-01: locked the former contractor jpark (sudo with a password, not in the staff list, brute-forced) and removed his WP administrator role. Removed deploy's sudo rsync (root via -e). larkspur-orders no longer runs the deploy-writable wp-config.php as root or evals its output. The mailing-export tool now has the user write the file (before, a symlink in the home folder let any user of it overwrite any file as root). Removed the old agency's unauthenticated must-use plugin (?asup=env showed DB settings). nginx refuses PHP under uploads. The internal maint.d steps are root-owned again (were deploy-writable). auth.log is 640 again (was world-readable). Grafana's SMTP password was identical to the deploy password; rotated smtp-password to separate them. ci-01: repo config with the GitHub token 640 root:developers (was world-readable); hooks root-owned; maint git gc runs as deploy with hooks off (was root on a developer-writable repo). db-01's backup key is now limited to write-only rrsync into /srv/backups, and its .ssh folder is root-owned. Release, dumps to ci-01, payouts, settle, orders and report jobs all verified working.
Recommendations: the deploy account still takes passwords from the internet and is brute-forced daily. Move the old monitoring box to a key, then disable password auth for deploy. Also remove kowens' 'old-laptop' key.

Compromise: someone was using Mia Fischer's (mfischer) web-01 password. Evidence: password logins from 107.77.170.208 at 14:05, 14:09 and 14:13. She had never used that address in 14 days, and she was also active from her home address (67.180.67.206) at 14:07. The sessions read the access log, exported the newsletter list (41 customers, names and emails) and printed the whole file (she normally looks at 5 lines), then ran `sudo -n -l` and `ls -la ~` to see what the account can do. Confirmation: after I rotated the password, the real Mia failed with the old one from home at 14:16, then logged in with her own iPad key (from 172.56.158.70) and has worked normally since. Containment: killed the intruder's sessions, rotated mfischer's password (rotate-secret staff-password; the help desk gives her the new one), dropped 107.77.170.208 in web-01's firewall (no packets since). Scope: only web-01; mfischer has no account on db-01 or ci-01, and the address appears nowhere else. Her keys and crontab are unchanged and she left no other files. Her sudo is only the export tool. Its root hole was closed before the 14:13 session, and the export log shows no misuse. She can read no secrets (payments.ini, backup, GitHub, bucket and Grafana secrets are root/grafana-only; no secrets in the logs she can read), so no shop secret needed rotating. Data exposed: the newsletter customer list. Please ask Mia how her password may have leaked and consider telling those customers.
Not intrusions: deploy password logins from 35.196.129.99 (the old monitoring box; only sudo larkspur-restart) and from Maria's 73.162.70.232; internet brute force against deploy, jpark, root and others (all failed); Grafana file-read probes from 159.89.112.12 (404, patched); Tor POSTs to the rentals form (normal).
Weaknesses fixed, everything else still working (release every 3 min, dumps to ci-01, payouts, settle, exports, site): web-01: locked the former contractor jpark (sudo with a password, not in the staff list) and removed his WP administrator role. Removed deploy's sudo /usr/bin/rsync (root shell). larkspur-orders no longer runs the deploy-writable wp-config.php as root or evals its output. The mailing-export tool now has the user write the file (a symlink in the home folder gave root file writes). Removed the old agency's unauthenticated must-use plugin agency-support.php (kept in /root/disabled). nginx refuses PHP in uploads. The internal maint.d steps ci-01 can run as root are root-owned again. auth.log is 640 again. Grafana's SMTP password was identical to the deploy password; rotated it (smtp-password). ci-01: repo config with the GitHub token is no longer world-readable (640 root:developers); hooks root-owned; the root maintenance job runs git gc as deploy with hooks off. db-01's backup key is limited to write-only rrsync into /srv/backups, and its .ssh is root-owned.
Still to do (needs people): staff passwords work from the internet, and that is how this happened. Move staff, and the old monitoring box's deploy login, to keys, then turn off SSH password auth. Remove kowens' unused 'old-laptop' key. Backups in /root and the fixed scripts are noted on each host.
